atoms.text: Slavery often separated enslaved people from their families, so they created new kinship-bonds and community. This also led to communities creating new forms of religious practices. They were influenced by West African religions of Igbo, Akan, Asante and Kongo origin.

atoms.text: In Jamaica, this spiritual resistance fuelled slave revolts like the Tacky's War in 1760. To regain control afterwards, the British administration installed bans on those practices. Despite this, many held onto their religious traditions and a minority of people still practice them today.

b: ++West African religions influenced Jamaican religious practices.
++Enslaved Jamaicans started a revolt against the British.
The Jamaicans published newsletters against enslavement.
The British forced all enslaved Jamaicans to become Christian.

atoms.text: British abolition activism led to the end of the British Slave Trade in 1807 and slavery in 1833. The campaign was led largely by English Quakers, reform-minded MPs and some middle-class citizens.

hint.text:
MP steht für Member of Parliament.
Quakers sind eine protestantische Glaubensgemeinschaft. Sie glauben, dass alle Menschen eine Verbindung zu Gott aufbauen können und deswegen gleichwertig sind.
hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>MP</lang> steht für <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>Member of Parliament. Quakers</lang> sind eine protestantische Glaubensgemeinschaft. Sie glauben, dass alle Menschen eine Verbindung zu Gott aufbauen können und deswegen gleichwertig sind.
hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.text: Christianity was used both to defend slavery and to oppose it: many slaveholders and pro-slavery writers invoked Christian language to justify slavery. Reformers, however, argued that slavery violated human equality and Christian morality.

hint.text:

to oppose – sich widersetzen
slaveholders – Sklavenhalter
to violate – verletzen

atoms.text: The Mau Mau War began as an anti-colonial uprising, mainly led by Kenyan Kikuyu fighters against British rule in the 1950s. They fought against land dispossession and forced labour. Britain answered with a brutal military campaign. The conflict ended in 1960 and became one of the key struggles that resulted in Kenya's independence in 1963.

b: The Kenyans agreed to work for the British Empire.
++The British military reacted with brutal warfare.
